content:
Facts: Plaintiff challenged 2013 holographic will appointing wife sole heir claiming apocrypha; alternatively sought property-sale ineffectiveness or damages; asserted second 2013 will appointing him heir valid; defendant-wife counterclaimed first will authentic, second will apocryphal and drawn by incapable person; double court-appointed expert determined first will (June) authentic while second will (September) involved multiple hands writing different sections.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic will validity requirements; nullity for form defects); established case law on progressive will-drafting (Cass. 2074/1985).
Interpretive Issues: Burden allocation proving holographic will authenticity/apocrypha; effect of court-appointed expert findings on authenticity determination; validity of property-sale when seller acquired ownership via subsequently-challenged will; whether holographic will progressively drafted with later additions constitutes single valid document; acceptance criteria for expert-report conclusions.
Principles Applied: Court-appointed expert responding to authenticity questions clarified factual-case terms enabling fact-ascertainment. First expert-opinion: June-2013 holographic will (content and signature) attributable to deceased, autograph. Second expert-opinion conclusion: September-2013 will drafting involved several hands; one hand wrote testamentary-wishes, another hand wrote single-line "Frosinone 3 September 2013" and signature. Conclusions fully acceptable as free from logical-flaws/contradictions; affirming June-2013 holographic will addressed to wife authentic, valid, fully-effective; subsequent September-2013 will written regarding brother apocryphal. First will valid complying all Art. 602 formal-requirements; consequence: property-sale fully valid/effective given defendant-transferor already owned apartment (50% undivided-ownership) purchased under legal-community regime with husband, acquiring sole-heir status. Conclusion rejects both June-2013 will-nullity claim and property-sale ineffectiveness claim, therefore return-to-estate claim; simultaneously accepts counterclaim declaring September-2013 will null per Art. 606 (formal-requirements lack). Alleged testamentary-incapacity claim unfounded absent technical-assessment; no grounds affirming incapacity. Main claim rejected, counterclaim upheld. No predetermined will-drafting timeframe requirement; holographic-will progressively-draftable; valid when testator uses own previously-handwritten notes, adding date/signature/intention-revealing expressions at later-date. Testator may affix date when testamentary-wishes consolidated; physical-condition variation between drafting-time and dating-time insufficient raising mental-capacity doubts existing at drafting-time.
